title: Honest Inference for Causal Derivatives under Nearly Touching Two-Branch Treatment-History Support
banked_reason: N-no-stat-frontier-advance — The exact known two-sheet, noiseless-chart, fixed-contact-order model yields a credible new specialization, but the proposed consequence beyond a bespoke weak-regressor regression experiment is not yet sufficient for field tier.
gap_reasons: N-no-stat-frontier-advance — The exact known two-sheet, noiseless-chart, fixed-contact-order model yields a credible new specialization, but the proposed consequence beyond a bespoke weak-regressor regression experiment is not yet sufficient for field tier; it needs a broader supported chart class, a genuine propensity-roughness frontier, or a demonstrated consequential application.
The present exact-family result is viable but below the enforced field novelty floor.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed a sound exact-family result for normal-derivative identification and weak-support inference on H=(X,±aX^k), then repaired the augmented potential-outcome model and its closest thin-support literature comparison. Three proposal versions could not lift the contribution above letter tier without relabeling coordinate transports as general geometry. A field-level successor would need a genuinely quantitative causal-Whitney modulus theory, a proved propensity-roughness phase diagram, or a consequential application rather than another restatement of the same two-sheet experiment.
tldr: For exact known two-branch treatment-history support, can a normal causal derivative retain honest, oracle-order inference when the branch propensity is unknown and the branches nearly touch? Continuous regular-kernel versions of support-local response parallel trends identify the causal trace; a split-sample contrast and bounded causal alternatives suggest a contact-order width frontier. The contribution sought is the fully feasible unknown-propensity theorem with constants uniform as the known branch separation shrinks, within this exact family.
gap: Classical Whitney/Glaeser geometry explains first-order visibility, and existing causal positivity-violation and honest-regression work addresses adjacent targets. The inspected results do not transfer their assumptions or conclusions to the exact two-branch panel normal derivative with shrinking separation and estimated allocation.
fill: Prove the law-defined causal trace reduction, a finite-sample envelope-conditional interval with explicit uniform training and denominator events, and a bounded full-observed-law lower bound for the exact chart.
